item.title: Red Sox have ‘massive human,’ former first-round pick as roster candidates
item.description: LAS VEGAS — The Rule 5 Draft didn’t take place during the 2021-22 offseason, the last time Major League Baseball owners locked out players. This offseason’s Rule 5 Draft again is in jeopardy with a lockout expected to begin at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. “We’re operating as though that would go on as normal,” Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow said at the GM Meetings. Teams have until Nov. 17 to add eligible players to their 40-man roster to protect them from being available to other teams in the draft. The Red Sox have several borderline candidates to be protected in Mikey Romero , Blake Wehunt , Brooks Brannon , Hayden Mullins , Johanfran Garcia , Braiden Ward , Angel Bastardo and Yordanny Monegro. Baseball America ranks Bastardo, who Boston re-signed to a minor league contract at the start of the offseason, the highest-ranked prospect of the group. It lists Bastardo No. 15 organizationally, Romero No. 18 and Wehunt No. 19. SoxProspects.com ranks Wehunt No. 13, Bastardo 18th and Romero 22nd. The Sox don’t have any obvious no-doubt-about-it additions. So although Breslow said Boston will operate as if the draft will happen, perhaps the Sox will take their chances and add nobody to the 40-man roster with roster spots limited anways this offseason. That said, Romero, Wehunt and Bastardo are all interesting names to watch at the deadline next Tuesday. Romero might be the most intriguing Rule 5 Draft eligible player of the group because of his background as a first-round draft pick. The Red Sox selected him 24th overall in 2022, he’s still young and injuries have limited his development time in the minors. There’s still plenty of room to improve with more reps. Meanwhile, the Red Sox have a shortage in starting pitching depth, making Wehunt and Bastardo potential additions. Bastardo pitched out of the bullpen for the WooSox in 2026 in his return from Tommy John surgery but had previously been a starter throughout his minor league career. Romero, who turns 23 in January, posted disappointing overall statistics in 113 games for Triple-A Worcester in 2026. He batted .239 with a .305 on-base percentage, .375 slugging percentage, .680 OPS and 30 extra-base hits in 490 plate appearances. The left-handed hitter’s OPS was 112 points higher against righties than lefties. But some of the advanced metrics told a more positive story. Romero had the second highest hard-hit percentage (41.7%) among Worcester players (minimum 120 plate appearances) behind only Mickey Gasper , who had a 46.5% hard-hit percentage in 238 plate appearances. He also trailed only Gasper in average exit velocity (90.8 mph) and adjusted exit velocity (92.5 mph) for WooSox hitters with 120 or more plate appearances. Additionally, he cut down on his strikeout percentage considerably, going from 30.2% with Worcester in 2025 to 21.0% in 2026. He closed out the year fairly strong, batting .270 with a .350 on-base percentage, .421 slugging percentage and .771 OPS in 143 plate appearances

item.title: What should the Oregon Ducks expect from Michigan's defense?
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will host the Michigan Wolverines at Autzen Stadium this weekend for the first time since 2003, but this time it will be the Wolverines looking to play spoiler to the Ducks ' postseason hopes. Michigan has the defense to do it, while the offense remains another story . With NFL talent and plenty of veteran leadership on hand, the moment in front of a raucous Oregon crowd shouldn't be too threatening to the Wolverines, and it could create a low-scoring affair. Oregon is fresh off a 41-28 blowout on the road over Ohio State , while Michigan fell at home to rival Michigan State, 15-6, despite keeping the Spartans out of the end zone. Michigan's defense has been up to the task against everyone on the schedule this season, but Oregon presents the biggest test yet. Conversely, the Ducks have been rolling on offense after making changes to the coaching staff, but the Wolverines might be a difficult matchup. The Ducks don't have any margin for error, but the Wolverines have a stout secondary and an aggressive front seven that could slow Oregon's momentum. Let's take a look at what Michigan does on defense schematically, who to watch out for, and what the Ducks might be able to do to put points on the board. What does Michigan do well on defense? Defensive coordinator Jay Hill operates out of an aggressive 4-2-5 nickel defense that relies on simulated pressures and physical play in the secondary. The Wolverines play more man coverage than the average defense, relying on defensive backs getting their hands on receivers to force them off their lines and tip passes away before an elite wideout has a chance. Michigan has limited opponents to 154.8 passing yards per game, fifth-best in the country. When playing zone coverage, Michigan runs plenty of different pressures while having an experienced front four that can get after the quarterback by itself. The Wolverines play out of the nickel to allow an extra rusher in different looks, and when a team comes out in 12 personnel (one running back, two tight ends), the defense often shifts into a 4-3 look to help stop the run. That balance has helped Michigan rank among the best defenses in the country, limiting opponents to just 16.2 points per game (16th in the nation) and 100.6 rushing yards per game (17th). Players to Know DL John Henry Daley John Henry Daley was the biggest transfer portal acquisition in the offseason for Michigan, following Kyle Whittingham from Utah, where he was a first-team All-American last season. Daley has picked up where he left off, leading the Wolverines with six sacks and nine tackles for loss. Michigan has several good pass rushers up front, including Dom Nichols and Tariq Boney, but Daley is by far the biggest threat that the Ducks will need to keep an eye on. He had his best game of the season last week against Michigan State, racking up eight tackles, two sacks and a forced fumble. item.description: LAS VEGAS — For a few minutes Wednesday it was as if the security folks at the Aria Resort & Casino thought the baseball lockout already began. Veteran agent Scott Boras, who traditionally speaks to the media gathering at the annual General Manager meetings, set up a press conference for more than 100 reporters, complete with a Boras Corporation backdrop, only for hotel security to intervene and let his staff know it couldn't occur on the second floor of the hotel near the convention center. It was shifted to the first floor, away from the meeting rooms. First on the north side of the hall, and then shifted to the south side. Finally, after about a 15-minute delay, it began with Boras speaking for 52 minutes about his own clients, particularly two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal , the urgency that many deals will be done before the Dec. 1 lockout, and then expressed his vehement opposition against the idea of a salary cap. The most humorous moment came not with Boras’ puns, but when his cell phone rang while speaking. He looked at his cell phone, moved the ringer to silent, and said, “Just another owner begging to meet with Skubal." The Los Angeles Dodgers , New York Mets , San Diego Padres and Toronto Blue Jays already have confirmed appointments. Boras expects Skubal to sign before the Dec. 1 lockout knowing that if there’s a salary cap, or at least further tax restrictions, it’s better to land a deal now while there’s uncertainty on how the landscape will look in the future. Yes, and it starts with Skubal, who’s seeking a deal that will exceed $325 million, making him the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history. item.title: Lewis Hamilton demands Israel allows aid into Gaza after Rafah visit: ‘No excuse’
item.description: Lewis Hamilton has said Israel must let aid trucks into Gaza in a passionate Instagram post, a day after he toured the Rafah border crossing in Egypt . The seven-time Formula One world champion arrived in El Arish on Tuesday, and during the trip he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it is sent into Gaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses. Following the visit, Hamilton took to Instagram to send a clear message to Israel and his 44.4 million followers. "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling. It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less," the Ferrari driver wrote on Instagram. Israel strongly denies accusations of genocide and says its military campaign in Gaza targets Hamas militants. Hamilton described seeing food trucks lined up and ready to go at the border that were regularly held up or faced major delays. Hamilton poses for a photo with Egyptian Red Crescent members (AFP/Getty) He said that at a nearby logistics centre, items had been rejected for "crazy reasons", including sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, and footballs for children. "Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse," he said. "I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away." Hamilton, 41, is an advocate for humanitarian causes. In 2021 he founded Mission 44, a charity that supports young people and works to improve their access to education and employment. The Brit is currently fourth in the F1 drivers’ standings, but is just a point behind third-placed George Russell, while he is only 18 adrift of Max Verstappen in second. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli has already won the world title, becoming F1’s youngest champion in the process, with three races of the season remaining. The next F1 race is due to be held in Las Vegas on 21 November, before the season concludes in the Middle East with back-to-back races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Pep Guardiola set to become United States' top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United close in
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-MAN CITY-PSG - AFP Pep Guardiola is set to be the United States' top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino, with the Argentine closing in on the Manchester United job. The former Manchester City boss came close to taking charge of Italy in the summer and has long been intrigued by working in America, having previously described the USA as "fascinating" for building a long-term project. United States set sights on Guardiola Pochettino is with his United States players ahead of their CONCACAF Nations League fixtures against Haiti this fortnight, but he is expected to join Manchester United once those games are over. United moved closer to appointing the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss after reaching a verbal agreement with him on Wednesday. That would leave the US needing a new head coach, and according to The Athletic , they will make Guardiola their top target. The Spaniard won the Champions League and six Premier League titles at City, having previously enjoyed huge success with Barcelona and Bayern Munich. Guardiola came close to taking Italy job Guardiola has previously shown interest in moving into international football, and he came so close to becoming Italy manager in the summer that he was writing down line-ups before deciding against the role. Italian Football Federation technical director Paolo Maldini later resigned after a move to appoint Andrea Pirlo also collapsed because of his commercial links with a Russian betting company. Maldini told Corriere della Sera: "[Guardiola] is the coach who best embodies technical, attacking football. He had expressed the idea of wanting to coach a national team to some friends. We went to meet him in Barcelona, we had lunch together, we talked for an entire day. He was very tempted. He came very close to accepting. He even started writing line-ups down on sheets of paper." Guardiola intrigued by USA project Guardiola is reported to have spoken to officials at the US national team in the past and is intrigued by the idea of working in America, having lived briefly in New York after leaving Barcelona in 2012. He was said to have been approached in 2024 before Pochettino was appointed, and he wished his fellow coach well when he took the job. Guardiola said at the time: "I wish him and the USA - I have friends there - the best of luck. I know he's a top-class manager." He has also previously been quoted as saying: "The USA is fascinating to try and build a project for many years and being able to get the national team to the next step. The potential with the USA is there for the amount of people and sports and so on." What next for Manchester United and the USA? item.title: Detroit Lions Re-Sign Familiar Face Prior to Germany Trip
item.description: The Detroit Lions are bringing back a familiar face just days before their Week 10 showdown against the New England Patriots in Germany. According to the NFL Transactions Log, Detroit has re-signed Jackson Meeks to its practice squad. The move comes just two days after the Lions waived Meeks to make room for veteran safety Andre Cisco, whom Detroit acquired from the New York Jets ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. Now, Meeks is back in the organization, giving Detroit additional offensive depth as the team prepares for the second half of the season. Aug 29, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Detroit Lions tight end Jackson Meeks (13) reacts after scoring a touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts during the first half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Bring Back Jackson Meeks Meeks originally joined the Lions as an undrafted free agent out of Syracuse following the 2025 NFL Draft. The former wide receiver eventually transitioned into a hybrid tight end role, showcasing his versatility during training camp and the preseason. His development was impressive enough that he earned a spot on Detroit’s initial 53-man roster heading into the 2026 season. According to his official NFL player statistics , Meeks has recorded one reception for eight yards during the regular season. The Lions waived Meeks on Monday as part of the roster adjustment following the Cisco trade, a move also documented on the team’s official transaction page . His reported return to the practice squad allows Detroit to retain a developmental player who already understands the offense. Lions Preparing for Germany Showdown Detroit enters Sunday’s matchup against New England with a 6-2 record and a four-game winning streak. While Meeks’ practice squad signing is unlikely to make headlines nationally, it gives the Lions another familiar option should injuries create a need for additional offensive depth. For Meeks, it’s another opportunity to continue developing with the organization that gave him his first NFL opportunity. And for the Lions, it’s a low-risk move to retain a player they clearly saw potential in during training camp.

item.title: Can Bear Bachmeier bounce back against Baylor?
item.description: BYU Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier (47) jumps during a football game against the Utah Utes at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News Three days after throwing four interceptions in BYU’s 28-20 loss at now-No. 2 Utah, sophomore quarterback Bear Bachmeier met with reporters Tuesday after practice and called the subpar performance a “great learning experience” and a “humbling experience.” Bachmeier also dispelled internet rumors that he sustained an injury that limited what he could do in Saturday’s rivalry game at Rice-Eccles Stadium, saying he is “feeling good physically” and accustomed to taking hits in every game. “You gotta be tough,” he said. “… We got Baylor on Saturday, and we got to bounce back. … The locker room (mood) was tough. But yeah, we got a team coming in here on Saturday, and we got to be ready to play.” The No. 10 Cougars (7-2, 4-2) host unranked Baylor 6-3, 4-2) on Saturday, and the sobering thought for Bachmeier and the BYU offense is that the Bears have the No. 18 scoring defense in the country, giving up just 17 points per game. “They are physical and they know their scheme well and they just play ball,” Bachmeier said. Offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick also spoke to reporters Tuesday and said that Bachmeier was one of the reasons why the Cougars gave the Utes their biggest test of the season, throwing for 272 yards and rushing for 59 in BYU’s first loss to Utah since 2019. “He just had a tough day, man. Bear’s been such a good player for us and is still a good player,” Roderick said. “I mean, he made so many good plays in that game that gave us a chance to win, and then just a few bad plays that were costly. But that hasn’t diminished our faith in him one bit.” Monday, offensive lineman Bruce Mitchell said teammates began rallying around Bachmeier and other guys who struggled in front of 52,901 and a national television audience of more than 4 million immediately after the game and continued that throughout the weekend. “I don’t think anybody was too stoked in the locker room following the game, but man, I know Bear, I know the character he has, and I know he’s going to bounce back,” Mitchell said. “It was not just his fault. He’s taking a lot of heat on it, and taking a lot of heat in the media. He’s taking it personally. “You know, if we are able to run the ball better, I am sure he will be able to pass the ball more efficiently,” Mitchell continued, lamenting BYU’s 119 rushing yards. “He’s going to bounce back. item.title: Where Will It End? 2nd Tier Schools Want a 2nd CFP Tournament!
item.description: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images West Virginia athletic director Wren Baker stated that “Yes, there would be a market” for a Group of Six football playoff. This comment came on Wednesday as schools weigh the impact of the upcoming 24-team College Football Playoff . The expansion starts in 2027, and it threatens to push smaller conference teams into a crowded field. Baker’s words signal that schools are already looking for a way to keep their top teams playing for a title. Memphis AD Pushes for Second Chance Memphis athletic director Ed Scott told USA TODAY Sports he has spoken with peers about the idea. “I’ve talked to some other ADs about it,” Scott said during a wide-ranging interview on Wednesday. He does not want Memphis to lose its spot in the big 24-team field, but he sees value in a separate tournament for the rest of the Group of Six. The plan would let a top team from each of the six conferences enter an eight-team bracket. This would happen after the main playoff field is set. It works much as the NIT does for college basketball teams that miss the main NCAA Tournament. Scott noted that the current bowl system is losing its appeal with players. “Bowl games are getting harder to get buy-in from your players, especially after the holidays,” the Memphis AD acknowledged. Players often want to go home for the break, but a championship game offers a better reason to stay. The new playoff would give those teams a real shot at a title rather than a generic bowl matchup. The new playoff could change how the postseason feels for fans in smaller markets. ESPN Paid More to Keep Control The push for expansion came despite strong opposition from the network that holds the rights. Pete Thamel of ESPN reports that the network will pay an additional $345 million per year, on average, for the expanded playoff over the next five years. The deal was finalized on Monday, and it removes the Power 4 conference championship games. ESPN agreed to the terms because the conferences demanded a larger field. The network wanted to keep ownership of the event rather than risk a lowball offer from a competitor. item.title: Pediatric patients cross finish line ahead of Charlotte Marathon
item.description: Ryder crosses the finish line as the 2026 Charlotte Marathon's first "first finisher" at Novant Health Hemby Children's Hospital. About 13,000 runners are expected to hit the streets for the Charlotte Marathon this Saturday, and all of the proceeds benefit Novant Health Hemby Children’s Hospital. While the runners prepare for Saturday’s big and long race, the kids here who will benefit from it were the first finishers to cross the line on Wednesday. Ryder is one of the kids at Novant Health Hemby Children’s Hospital. He’s been cooped up in a room for two days, which is tough for him and his mom. “It’s stressful. And overwhelming. A lot. And then to be confined to 4 walls makes it a little worse. So events like this are really nice,” said Vanessa Villanueva, Ryder’s mom. The Charlotte Marathon is Saturday , and all the proceeds benefit the children’s hospital. One of the child life specialists who helps these kids is also running in the half-marathon Saturday. “It is my first one! Me and a lot of my coworkers are running, so we’re really excited to give back to Novant and help support our patients through that,” said Avery Bradford at Novant Health Hemby Children’s Hospital. “Are you excited or nervous?” asked Channel 9’s Evan Donovan. “Both, for sure both,” Bradford said. For the first time, the marathon is being put on by the Charlotte Sports Foundation, which also puts on the Duke’s Mayo Classic and the Charlotte Invitational. They hope this becomes a community event, not just for runners. “Yes, so that’s something we’re trying to bring forth this year is really capture all the different neighborhoods the runners will be going through and get the community out and cheering. And maybe this can be something the community can own and look forward to every year,” said Kaleah Ellerbe with the Charlotte Sports Foundation. As kids enjoyed blowing bubbles and making signs for the race, Ryder became the first finisher to cross the line. “Ladies and gentlemen, for the 2026 Charlotte Marathon, he’s fast as can be, coming down the chute, he’s our first first-finisher, Ryder,” an announcer said. The Charlotte Marathon is this Saturday morning, and everyone is encouraged to come out and run or cheer. “What I love is it starts in Uptown and then you get to go into Eastover and look at all of the big houses and hear 10,000 footsteps and you get to go through Myers Park, Dilworth, South End, Plaza Midwood, NoDa, all these really unique neighborhoods that make Charlotte special,” said Miller Yoho with the Charlotte Sports Foundation. Channel 9 will have a full wrap-up in our Charlotte Marathon special at noon on Sunday, so if you’re at the race on Saturday, you can still watch.

item.title: UAlbany men's basketball sunk by 3-point barrage in loss to Dartmouth
item.description: UAlbany freshman Tyler Jones drives to the basket in front of Dartmouth sophomore Anton Strelnikov on Wednesday, Nov. 14, 2026, at the Broadview Center in Albany, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) ALBANY - The University at Albany men's basketball team knew from its scouting report that Dartmouth wasn't going to be shy about letting the 3-point shots fly in Wednesday's matinee matchup at Broadview Center. When the Big Green started out red-hot from beyond the arc, it put UAlbany in a hole the Great Danes were unable to dig out of - even with a spirited late rally. Dartmouth made its first five 3-point attempts and 7-of-8 overall to start the game, and finished the afternoon 13-of-30 from deep in an 85-76 nonconference win. "They believe so heavily in the 3," UAlbany coach Dwayne Killings said of the Big Green. "So they just keep shooting, and I think they shot themselves into a pretty good game today." Killings lamented the defensive struggles that UAlbany (2-2 overall) had against a Dartmouth (3-1) team that entered Wednesday averaging 32.3 3-point attempts per game, but was shooting just 30.9% from beyond the arc. Against UAlbany, with the Great Danes struggling to cover in man-to-man sets and forced to rely on a 1-3-1 zone, Dartmouth shot 43.3% from deep. "We need to clean up everything defensively," said UAlbany freshman guard Tyler Jones, who finished with 15 points and eight assists. "We have to be dogs on the court. We knew that they shoot 3s," added freshman forward Erwann Bussing, who had his best game in a UAlbany uniform with 11 points. "We can't let them in the first half be 7-of-13. We have to be better than that." Dartmouth's hot shooting start allowed the Big Green to forge a 49-36 halftime lead. The advantage eventually pushed to as many as 18 points with 8:53 left in the second half before UAlbany finally made a run. The Great Danes put a serious scare into the Big Green, with a 10-0 run making it a 78-74 game when Bussing scored with 53 seconds left. But on Dartmouth's ensuing trip down the floor, the Big Green burned nearly the entire 30-second shot clock before Cameron Hiatt drained a corner 3 that iced the win. "We trapped, and they got out. We stayed solid, and then they bury a 3 that killed us," Killings said. "I thought we needed one more stop, and then it's a one-possession game. … They executed better than we did." Dan Civello scored 16 points to lead three Dartmouth players in double figures. Ten different players scored at least four points for the Big Green, and coach Brett MacConnell deployed a substitution pattern that essentially split his team into two five-man units who played together nearly exclusively. Ollie Engen finished with a game-high 18 points and added five assists for UAlbany. Jones' 15-point night was the fourth straight double-figure scoring game for the highly touted freshman , while Bussing and Abdoulaye Fall each scored 11. item.title: Manchester City may have identified the striker they want to support Erling Haaland
item.description: Manchester City may have identified the striker they want to support Erling Haaland Perhaps the most difficult task for the Manchester City hierarchy when constructing Enzo Maresca’s squad is finding quality cover for Erling Haaland. Haaland will play the majority of games up front for City. Given his stature in the game and his goalscoring prowess, Haaland is almost a permanent fixture in City’s starting lineup. Finding a player who will be happy to be used sparingly and as Haaland’s backup is no easy task. There are two routes for City to take to find quality cover for Haaland. They could find a young striker to develop behind Haaland. The alternative is to find an experienced striker who is happy to prove himself at City by playing a vital role for Enzo Maresca’s side. Club Brugge’s impressive young striker Nicolo Tresoldi fits the bill as a young striker that City could target in January. However, a new report has named Bournemouth’s hard-working striker Evanilson as a potential transfer target for Manchester City in January. Evanilson ticks the box of an experienced striker who could provide quality cover for Erling Haaland if City did pursue a move in January. Manchester City have reportedly been tracking the performances of Evanilson in recent weeks. Mark Brus has reported via his exclusive Daily Briefing column that Manchester City, alongside Arsenal, are keeping tabs on the performances of Evanilson for Bournemouth. On City’s interest in Evanilson, Brus reports: “ Manchester City’s technical staff and scouting department have been closely monitoring Evanilson in recent weeks. Internal technical evaluations suggest that he’s seen as someone who could adapt quickly to Enzo Maresca’s system and add significant dynamism to the frontline. ” It is further reported that Arsenal and Manchester City could be prepared to move for Evanilson in January. Brus adds that Bournemouth could slap a €60 million price tag on their Brazilian striker to fend off any interest from clubs. Lastly, it is also reported that Evanilson could be interested in a move away from Bournemouth if the right opportunity arises. In terms of finding a striker who could come in and do a job for City, Evanilson ticks all of the right boxes. Evanilson could be the ideal striker for Manchester City to target. The 27-year-old Brazilian striker is a proven performer. During his time at FC Porto, he scored 60 goals in 154 appearances. After signing for Bournemouth, Evanilson has scored 25 goals and added 14 assists in 86 appearances. Those numbers don’t jump off the page. However, Evanilson is a proven goalscorer although there is more to his game. Evanilson is very good at dropping into space between the midfield and defence to link Bournemouth’s play. item.description: The Notre Dame legend joined ESPN’s College GameDay, celebrated with Irish fans, and helped put a charitable spotlight on a memorable Notre Dame–Miami weekend. There are certain people who can return to Notre Dame at any time, for any reason, and immediately make a special weekend even more memorable. Joe Montana is definitely one of them. And when you combine a Notre Dame legend, a little Guinness, ESPN’s College GameDay, a showdown with Miami, and a generous charitable donation, you’ve got the ingredients for one pretty unforgettable Saturday in South Bend. Of course, it doesn’t hurt when the Fighting Irish finish the day with a victory over the No. 1 team in the country! Before Notre Dame defeated Miami 31–24 on Saturday, November 7, Montana returned to South Bend as a Guinness ambassador for a weekend that celebrated football, friendship, tradition, and giving back. There was the famous comeback against Houston in the 1979 Cotton Bowl, when Montana helped rally the Irish to a 35–34 victory in bitterly cold conditions, and of course, there were all those unforgettable moments that followed with the San Francisco 49ers. But no matter how many championships he won or how many legendary plays he made, Montana’s connection to Notre Dame has always remained part of his story. So when ESPN brought College GameDay to South Bend for the highly anticipated Notre Dame–Miami matchup, having Montana back on campus seemed especially fitting. item.title: Barcelona star advised to consider move away from the club: ‘Using him like a yo-yo’
item.description: Barcelona star advised to consider move away from the club: ‘Using him like a yo-yo’ Barcelona star Frenkie de Jong has this week been urged to take into serious consideration his long-term future in Catalunya’s capital. This comes after the Dutchman was tested in a surprise new role this past weekend. Barcelona are of course fresh off a crucial three-point haul on Sunday, when they put Diego Simeone’s Atlético Madrid to the sword by two goals to one in Spain’s capital. The aforementioned De Jong was forced to make do with a place on the bench at the Metropolitano, before ultimately being introduced during the 2nd-half. Rather than in his favoured role in the middle of the park, though, the 29-year-old was asked to fill an unfamiliar position at right-back. This is not the first time De Jong has been asked to take to the pitch in a changed role this season, having also recently filled in at the heart of defence. And it is precisely these changes which have this week seen the former Ajax man urged to take into consideration a potential move away from the Camp Nou. Speaking during an appearance on Ziggo Sport program Rondo (as cited by Diario Sport ), ex-Dutch international Khalid Boulahrouz made use of the opportunity to send some advice De Jong’s way: “If I were Frenkie, I would start slowly thinking about what I want. They’re using him like a yo-yo. This time it was ten minutes, but next time they might say he’s already proven he can do it and that, if needed, he’ll play half an hour at right-back!” Boulahrouz continued: “Then you have to start asking yourself: is this what I want? He’s a midfielder, and that’s where he plays best. He could also play as a centre-back, but if now he has to move to right-back…” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Four starting offensive linemen limited as Bills prepare for Jets
item.description: Bills offensive line work through blocking drills. The Buffalo Bills just finished a very tough stretch of their schedule, and they did it while juggling injuries and playing roster-Jenga to keep the right personnel on the game day roster. Now they enter Week 10 as the league’s top team, the AFC’s number one seed and in control of their post-season destiny. While the next couple of weeks, on paper, look a little easier than the last five, facing division rivals – regardless of their record – is never a walk in the park. However, Buffalo knows what they are facing. They are as familiar with their opponent as possible. So, if they need to take an extra day or two to let some veterans get some rest, get the new guy up to speed, and let a few people work out the kinks, bumps, and bruises, this would be the time. However, instead, the Bills listed everyone as participating in Wednesday’s first practice of the week. Wednesday injury report pic.twitter.com/DBuzVeU6Mv — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 11, 2026 Limited Participation OL Alec Anderson (ankle) CB Christian Benford (wrist) T Spencer Brown (ankle) T Dion Dawkins (rib) TE Dalton Kincaid (ankle) C Conner McGovern (neck) Four of the Bills’ five starting offensive linemen are on this list. Not the best situation for you if your name is Josh Allen. But it’s good to know Anderson and Dawkins, who both missed Monday night in Minnesota, are on the mend. It’s also good – maybe – that Brown’s back isn’t an issue any longer. But sometimes a pain you know is easier to manage than one that’s new. Buffalo signed guard Nick Broeker to the practice squad this morning. We thought that wasn’t a great sign for Anderson. Now it looks like the move may have had something to do with the fact that the entire O-line is banged up. Full Participation DL Greg Gaines (calf) DB Jordan Hancock (IR) G Ar’maj Reed-Adams (back/elbow) DL T.J. Sanders (shoulder) WR Tyrell Shavers (PUP) The Bills aren’t done performing roster gymnastics just because the trade deadline has passed. Both Hancock and Shavers are gearing up for a return to the 53-man roster. Buffalo has one more week to figure out what to do with Shavers and a few days later they will have to make room for Hancock. This will be something to keep our eyes on over the next week. What to watch It’s important to keep in mind that this was a walk through practice and these designations are what the training and coaching staff anticipates a player’s participation would have been had it been a full practice. The real test will come tomorrow. Pads, routes, coverages, the whole thing – that will definitely tell us more about how the Bills are looking ahead of their trip to MetLife Stadium on Sunday.

item.title: Lions' Mahogany mum on reason for benching, says it won't happen again
item.description: ALLEN PARK — Christian Mahogany didn’t want to say much about what happened to cause him to lose his starting job on the offensive line prior to Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins . But as Mahogany returned to his first-team role at left guard in practice Wednesday, following a disciplinary benching for violating team rules, according to Dan Campbell, the third-year pro insisted “it won’t happen again.” More: Lions' Dan Campbell: Ball in Christian Mahogany's court after benching “You just gotta (take) it on the chin,” said Mahogany, a second-year starter who was limited to a handful of special-teams snaps in Miami. “That’s how I am. I’m not a person that ... I’m not going to sulk, and it sucked not being out there because I let my teammates down. I don’t want to do that. So I did, and that’s on me.” Campbell has declined to elaborate on the reasons for Mahogany’s punishment, explaining “that’s really between us.” “That’s why we have team rules and we’ve all got to abide by them,” Campbell said. “And if it’s broken multiple times, then you do something about it.” Mahogany, who didn’t speak to reporters after Sunday’s game, also declined to shed any light on the rules violations Wednesday, saying, “He already said he’s not going to disclose it, so I’m not going to disrespect my head coach to disclose it in any way.” But the decision was made prior to the team’s trip to Miami that Miles Frazier would start in his place against the Dolphins, “so it wasn’t a big surprise to me,” said Mahogany, whose training-camp battle for the starting job at left guard never really materialized after injuries to center Cade Mays and veteran guard Ben Bartch in August. Frazier struggled in his first career start Sunday, particularly in the first half, allowing multiple pressures as Jared Goff was sacked three times and the Lions mustered just 120 yards of offense. Mahogany, who missed the Week 2 loss at Buffalo with a hip injury, currently ranks as the league’s 10 th -best guard this season, according to Pro Football Focus. So with last week’s discipline behind them, Campbell said the plan was for Mahogany to “start with the first unit” this week, adding after the team held a walkthrough practice Wednesday that “he was good this morning.” “I had to grow up and I had to stop breaking team rules,” Mahogany said. “So it is what it is. I let my teammates down. I let my organization down. And it won’t ever happen again. … “It’s just who you have to be. That’s all it is. I’m just going to have to be the same person every day.” jniyo@detroitnews.com @johnniyo This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Lions' Mahogany mum on reason for benching, says it won't happen again
